definitions.title: Definition of an Antiderivative
definitions.latex: F'(x) = f(x) \implies \int f(x) \, dx = F(x) + C
definitions.statement: A function F is an antiderivative of f on an interval I if F'(x) = f(x) for all x in I. The collection of all antiderivatives of f is its indefinite integral, denoted int f(x) dx = F(x) + C where C is an arbitrary constant of integration.
conditions: C is an arbitrary real constant
definitions.explanation: Two antiderivatives of the same function on an interval differ by at most a constant: F(x) - G(x) = C.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Antidifferentiation is the inverse operation of differentiation.

definitions.title: Power Rule for Antiderivatives
definitions.statement: To antidifferentiate a power of x (other than -1), increment the exponent by 1 and divide by the new exponent.
conditions: n != -1 (when n = -1, int (1/x) dx = ln|x| + C)
definitions.explanation: Direct inverse of the differentiation power rule.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Add 1 to the exponent and divide by the new exponent.
